blocking_variables.detail: CustomerGroup rule's customer_group_ids array lives in the serialized preferences blob, not a dedicated join table. Confirmed 2026-09-11: likely preference key customer_group_ids (an array of spree_customer_groups.id values -- that table and spree_customer_group_users, which record actual customer<->group membership, are real, normalized tables in this schema; only the promotion rule's own list of TARGETED group ids is still blob-serialized, not the groups themselves). Less certain than the amount/operator keys above -- current Spree source names the accessor preferred_customer_group_ids, which may reflect a newer version than this schema snapshot; not verified against a real row.

existence check, unchanged by the redesign. Re-examined 2026-09-11: unlike operatorMin/amountMin/operatorMax/amountMax, this one stays genuinely uncertain even with the real preference keys confirmed -- ItemTotal declares amount_min/amount_max with hard non-null defaults, so a plain 'is the key present' test would always be true regardless of whether an admin actually configured a max threshold, and no real sample promotion_rules row was available to tell what 'amountMaxSet' is actually meant to distinguish (a sentinel value? a second rule instance existing at all?). Left unresolved rather than guessing a specific boolean test with no way to check it.
